title: Lower norm-six target denominator from 256 to 64 (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Reduce the sufficient common target denominator for the fixed P48p norm-six feature construction from 256 to 64, retaining 19,600 factor pairs and integral source features. Claim type: scoped written algebraic proof with an exact finite pivot certificate and endpoint corroboration. The new source and target feature sets must be used together.

```text
26 diagonal-eight roots + 22 signed unit edges
    -> 48-column integral relation pivot, |det| = 1
    -> integral elimination multipliers
    -> 19,600 pairs with integral target numerators / 64
```

For every integral source x with x^T G x=6 and every integral target y, the new factorization equals `((x^T G y)^3-4*x^T G y)/192`. The proof is an exact polynomial substitution, without a full-shell enumeration. Discovery stopped at the first improved denominator.

Credit Krzysztof Wojt / #5143 for the predecessor stream and relation-column formulas; Cinna Davis / #2222 for the kernel, Gram and integer-valued features; Nick Petalas / #5084 for the term bound; Brian / #5132 for the concurrent explicit construction; David Ganz / #4494, DreamingOfClouds / #2244 and the retained P48p/lattice/kernel/chart lineage. Classical unimodular elimination and polynomial substitution retain their credit. Predecessor scientific executables were not imported or replayed.

## Evidence

- Before: #5143 and #5132 provide target numerators over 256 for their chosen retained feature sets.
- After: separate exact elimination gives determinant -1 for the new pivot. All 2,304 integral-inverse entries, 204 target fixtures, 84 complete kernel endpoints with 1,646,400 records and 24 off-shell polynomial identities with 470,400 records pass. Every feature family contributes nonzero terms in each off-shell case. There are 61 nonzero-term omission controls and nine rejecting boundary/solve controls.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized execution produce identical generated receipts. The two registered commands took 1.50 and 1.41 seconds locally, well below their 120-second timeouts. These are check-duration observations, not performance-improvement claims.
- Package metadata/pins, final registered replay, committed bytes and modes, declared source ancestry, official eight-payload-file export integrity and optimized read-only Git-free replay with empty PATH pass at head `3626b3318b801752d1cbf90ca625cf2fa88f3072`.

```sh

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/norm6-unit-pivot/verify.py

```

An equivalent CPython 3.12 path works elsewhere. Expected direct marker: `PASS_NORM6_UNIT_PIVOT`. `PROOF.md`, `SOURCES.json`, `TASK.json` and `VERIFY.json` state the exact proof, source pins, scope change, environment and replay contract. Receipts are generated from current hashes; none is handwritten.

Geometric interpretation and the binary chart remain cited premises. All five selected framework assumptions remain. No supplier admission, new kappa or selected-frontier change is requested. No selected scientific cold replay, physical/native suite, Lean or Docker was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.
